findings.title: Fork PR failure
findings.text:
The workflow triggers on `pull_request`, but its install step requires
`secrets.REQ_RELEASE_TOKEN`. GitHub does not pass secrets (other than `GITHUB_TOKEN`)
to a workflow triggered by a pull request from a fork, so the install exits with
"REQ_RELEASE_TOKEN is not set" and the `req-diff` check is red for every external
contributor. The adopter section presents `--fail-on` as the merge gate, so a team that
marks this check required can never merge a fork PR. This may be the intended
trade-off, but neither the workflow header nor the new `## On a pull request` section
mentions it; document the limitation (and how to handle it) so adopters are not surprised.

findings.title: Summary var unset
findings.text:
The step runs under `set -u` and appends with `>> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` without a
default. GitHub always sets that variable, but the file advertises itself as copyable to
`<removed forgejo workflow>`, and on a runner that does not set
`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (some Forgejo/act_runner versions, or a local `act`) the
unbound-variable error aborts the shell after `req diff` has already run, so a passing
diff (exit 0) still fails the step. Using `>> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"` would
keep a missing summary from turning the check red (the pin test still matches the name).
I could not confirm whether current Forgejo/act_runner sets the variable, so treat this
as a robustness concern.
